title: Remove the n-th node from the end of a list
summary: Unhook the n-th carriage from the end of a train in one walk, by sending a scout n carriages ahead.
goal: Unhook the n-th carriage counting from the end

examples.label: Remove 2nd from end
examples.explanation: Carriage 4 is second from the end.

examples.label: Only carriage
examples.explanation: Removing the only carriage leaves an empty train.

examples.label: Remove the last
examples.explanation: The last carriage is first from the end.

ladder.name: Copy into an array
ladder.idea: Copy the carriages into an array, delete position length − n, and rebuild the train.

ladder.name: Count, then walk
ladder.idea: Walk once to count the carriages, then walk again to the one before position L − n and unhook the next.
ladder.insight: We only need the length to know where to stop, not a copy of every carriage.

ladder.name: Send a scout ahead
ladder.idea: Start a scout n + 1 carriages ahead of a marker. Move both together; when the scout falls off the end, the marker is just before the carriage to unhook.
ladder.insight: Keeping a fixed gap of n between two walkers measures "n from the end" without knowing the length, so one walk is enough.

transfer.problem: Find the k-th last entry in a long log you can only read forwards, once.
transfer.explanation: Keep a second pointer k entries behind the first; when the first reaches the end, the second is the answer.

selfCheck: Uses a placeholder head, so removing the first carriage works.
Moves the scout n + 1 steps before moving both.

aka: Remove Nth Node From End of List
